title: Audit UI Changes
bottom_line: Run one command on your branch to get a private page of before and after screenshots of every screen that really changed.

sections.heading: One command starts the audit, and flags skip its questions

blocks.caption: Type this in Claude Code on the branch you want to audit. Every flag is optional.

blocks.title: What each flag does
rows: Which platforms to capture this run. Skips the platforms question.
How to compare the old and new version. Skips the baseline question.
Audit every screen, not only what changed since the last audited commit.
The PR number. Without it, the skill looks the PR up with `gh pr view`.
Where to publish the audit page. Skips the publish question.
Which themes to capture when dark mode is enabled. Skips the themes question.
Ask nothing. Use the passed flags, the config and the defaults.
The model for the helper subagents. The default is `haiku`.

blocks.title: Why it exists
blocks.text: Reviewers cannot see UI changes from a diff, and shared CSS or components change screens nobody meant to touch. This skill shows what the UI really looks like before and after the change.

blocks.title: Other ways it starts
blocks.text: The skill also starts when you ask for screenshots of UI changes, a visual audit, a visual regression check, a UI diff for a PR, before/after images, or to "show reviewers what the UI looks like". It also starts when templates, components, styles, screens or front-end code changed and reviewers need to see the result.

`/plan-tools:finalize-pr` offers to run it when a PR touches UI files, then calls it with `--unattended`. That run asks nothing and uses the passed flags, the config and the defaults. It makes no dark-mode offer, and a failed base falls back to `head-only`.

You can also use it to set up, refresh or inspect the `.ui-audit/` config and manifest in a repo. It works for web (Playwright, desktop and mobile emulation) and, for Capacitor/Expo apps, simulators and emulators.

sections.heading: Have the right tools ready before you run it

cards.title: GitHub CLI
cards.text: `gh` CLI, authenticated. It looks up the PR and writes the `ui-audit` commit status.

cards.title: Python with two packages
cards.text: Python 3 with `pip install pillow numpy`, for image diffing. If they are missing, the skill tells you to install them and stops.

cards.title: Web: Playwright CLI
cards.text: The Playwright CLI (`playwright-cli`, via the `playwright-cli` skill).

cards.title: To publish as artifact
cards.text: The Claude Code `Artifact` tool. Artifacts are private: reviewers see the audit after you share it from claude.ai.

cards.title: To publish to Cloudflare
cards.text: Node (`npx`, already needed for the Playwright CLI) to run `npx wrangler@4 pages deploy`. Nothing to install.

cards.title: Native apps (optional)
cards.text: Xcode with iOS simulators (`xcrun simctl`), or the Android SDK with an emulator and `adb`. Optionally `ffmpeg` to convert recordings. Untested on real apps.

blocks.title: Environment variables
items: None are needed to publish as a Claude artifact.
To publish to Cloudflare Pages, set `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` (scope Account > Cloudflare Pages > Edit).
Also set `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID` when the token reaches more than one account.
Or run `! npx wrangler login` once instead. The skill never logs in itself.
The plugin has no plugin settings. Per-repo choices live in `.ui-audit/config.json`.

blocks.title: A clean working tree
blocks.text: Each run needs a clean working tree (it ignores `.ui-audit/`). If you have uncommitted changes, it offers to commit them and stops if you say no. An unpushed HEAD is fine.

sections.heading: The first run interviews you and sets up the repo

blocks.title: What happens on the first run
blocks.caption: The skill offers discovered defaults, so you mostly confirm.

blocks.title: The interview questions, a few at a time
items: Which platforms does this repo ship (web, Capacitor, Expo/React Native)? Which should be enabled for audits?
How do I start the app locally (command, port, working directory)? How do I know it is ready?
Does the app need login? Provide a test account or storage-state, or should I use an existing dev-login route?
Is there seed/fixture data so screens look the same on every run? If not, which regions are dynamic (clocks, avatars, random content) and should be masked?
Feature flags or env vars that need to be on for the screens to render?
Viewports: keep desktop 1440x900 and mobile 390x844 (touch, DPR 3), or different?
Default baseline mode (base+head recommended).
Publish target: Claude artifact (default) or Cloudflare Pages. Only if Cloudflare, the Pages project name (default `<repo-name>-ui-audit`).
Only if dark mode was detected: capture dark too? Confirm the detected `dark_mode` method.

blocks.title: The screen list
blocks.text: Next it proposes a screen list (name, route, notable states such as empty, error, modal, open menu). You confirm, merge or drop entries. Admin and internal screens are skipped unless you want them.
With `--unattended`, the interview and the screen-list confirmation are skipped and the defaults are used.

sections.heading: Every run follows the same six steps

steps.title: Check the working tree is clean
steps.text: It ignores `.ui-audit/`. If files are listed, it offers to commit your changes, otherwise it stops.

steps.title: Load the config
steps.text: It loads `.ui-audit/config.json`. On the first run it interviews you, discovers screens, and writes the config and manifest.

steps.title: Find what changed
steps.text: `BASE` is the merge-base with the PR base branch, always the diff baseline. `LAST` is the last audited commit (a `ui-audit` commit status on the PR, else `last_audited_sha` in the manifest). `LAST` only picks which screens to re-capture.

steps.title: Answer the per-run questions
steps.text: Which platforms (if several are enabled), which baseline mode and where to publish. `hosting.target` in the config is the default, and `--publish` skips that question.

steps.title: Capture, compare and classify
steps.text: It picks screens from file hashes plus reasoning about ripples from shared files, captures base (git worktree) and head under identical conditions, diffs, classifies, and builds the audit page.

steps.title: Publish and return the link
steps.text: It publishes the audit and returns the URL (and the password, if any), ready for the PR body.

blocks.title: When a run stops early or widens
items: The run stops if nothing changed since `LAST`.
If the base branch moved since the last audit, the run is a full sweep.

blocks.title: What it never does
items: It never pushes, and commits only your uncommitted work in the first step when you say yes.
`.ui-audit/` changes are left in the working tree for you or finalize-pr to commit.
Images are never committed.

sections.heading: Pick a baseline mode: base+head is the only one that finds surprises

cards.title: base+head (default)
cards.text: Captures the old and new version of every affected screen, then shows only screens that really changed, side by side with a diff overlay.

points.text: The only mode that can find unintended changes

cards.title: head-only
cards.text: Captures only the new version. Use it for brand new UIs or when the base cannot run.

points.text: No diff and no way to tell what changed

cards.title: head+base-related
cards.text: Captures the new version of all affected screens, but the old version only for screens whose own files changed.

points.text: Faster than the default on large apps
Ripples on other screens have no before image, so are tagged `needs_review`

blocks.title: The questions asked at the start of each run
items: Platforms, only if more than one is enabled in config: which to capture this run (for example web, iOS simulator, Android emulator). Native captures are slower, so you pick.
Baseline mode, always (default `base+head`).
Viewports: confirm the configured ones (default desktop and mobile). Mobile is browser emulation on web.
Publish target, unless `--publish` is given or the run is unattended: `Claude artifact` or `Cloudflare Pages`, with the config's `hosting.target` (default `artifact`) preselected.
Themes, unless `--themes` is given, only if config has a `dark_mode` object (web only): `light+dark` (default) or `light` only. Dark doubles the captures, so `light` is offered for quick runs.

blocks.text: The remaining questions are asked together. A flag that answers a question skips it, and `--unattended` asks none of them.

sections.heading: Publish privately as a Claude artifact or on Cloudflare Pages

cards.title: Claude artifact (default)
cards.text: Private until you share it from claude.ai.

cards.title: Cloudflare Pages
cards.text: Published at `https://pr-<n>.<project>.pages.dev`.

points.text: On a private repo it sits behind a password
A public repo gets no password

blocks.title: The Cloudflare password
items: The password is the first 12 characters of the audited commit sha.
It is kept in the `ui-audit` commit status and the PR body.
Anyone with the link and password sees the screenshots.

blocks.title: Switching targets and fallback
items: Changing the target for a PR that already has an audit carries the earlier items over to the new target.
If the chosen target cannot publish, the skill offers the artifact instead or keeps a local `index.html` and a `report.md` for the PR comment.
Retention: none automatic. An artifact, Pages project or deployment is deleted only when you ask.

sections.heading: Dark mode is opt-in and catches colors that change in one theme

blocks.title: How a dark-mode run checks a screen
blocks.caption: A screen that changed in one theme but not the other may have a hardcoded color or a missing dark variant.

blocks.title: How dark mode works
items: Web apps with a dark theme (detected from `prefers-color-scheme`, `.dark`/`[data-theme]` selectors or Tailwind `darkMode`) can opt in via a `dark_mode` object in `.ui-audit/config.json`.
`false` means none or declined, and you are not asked again.
Each run then also captures every chosen state in dark (`<state>--dark`), diffs base vs head, and cross-checks light and dark.
Choose `light` only at the per-run question for quicker runs.

sections.heading: You get tagged screens, a reviewable page and a PR-ready summary

blocks.title: Each changed screen gets one tag and a one-line reason

cards.title: intentional
cards.text: The screen was touched by the diff itself and the visual change is plausible.

cards.title: unintended
cards.text: Reached only through shared files or ripple and nobody meant to change it, or the change contradicts the diff.

cards.title: needs_review
cards.text: The skill cannot tell.

blocks.title: The audit page
items: Unintended items are listed first, with the diff overlay.
The page opens in the view set by `report.default_view` (`slider`, `side` or `diff`, default `slider`) and also has a view picker.
Each card shows its audit history.
A per-browser "Mark reviewed", which clears when the card changes in a later audit.
A per-browser "Skip" that collapses a card to its title row; it also clears when the card changes.

blocks.title: What the skill returns to you
items: Config suggestions (merges, deleted-file removals).
The audit URL and the password, if any.
Counts of changed, unintended and needs-review screens.
The list of unintended items with reasons.
Which screens were reused, and which were skipped and why.
The `report.md` text as a ready PR comment, if hosting was unavailable.

blocks.text: It also records a `ui-audit` commit status on the PR head. This is fixed, because `finalize-pr` relies on it.

blocks.title: What the PR body gets
blocks.code:
## UI audit
Latest: https://claude.ai/artifact/<id>  (2 changed screens, 1 unintended)

blocks.title: Or, on Cloudflare Pages with a private repo
blocks.code:
## UI audit
Latest: https://pr-12.my-repo-ui-audit.pages.dev  (2 changed screens, 1 unintended)
Password: `3f9c1a7be204` (username: anything)

blocks.text: A later commit that only touches `about.html` re-captures `about` alone.

sections.heading: Defaults you can change, and what lives in the repo

rows: Publish as a private Claude artifact
Compare base and head (`base+head`), showing only screens that really changed
Light theme only; dark is captured too once the repo opts in with a `dark_mode` object in `.ui-audit/config.json`
Helper subagents run on the `haiku` model
Audit only what changed since the last audited commit
Record a `ui-audit` commit status on the PR head

blocks.title: Committed in your repo under .ui-audit/
items: `config.json`: platforms, launch command and base URL, login and seed data, hosting target and Cloudflare Pages project name (`hosting`), viewports (default desktop 1440x900 and mobile 390x844 with touch, via browser emulation), screens and states, masked regions, diff thresholds, default baseline mode, native device settings.
Platform ids in `config.json`: `web`, `capacitor-ios`, `capacitor-android`, `expo-ios`, `expo-android`.
`manifest.json`: maintained by the skill. Only screens whose hash changed are re-captured on repeat runs.

sections.heading: If something goes wrong, the skill says so and falls back

cards.title: No UI changes
cards.text: No UI changes in the diff and nothing shared changed.

points.text: Reports "no UI changes since `LAST`" and builds nothing

cards.title: App fails on base
cards.text: The app fails to start on base, and the skill says so.

points.text: Falls back to `head-only` for that platform after asking you
With `--unattended`, falls back without asking and notes it

cards.title: A recipe step fails
cards.text: A recipe step no longer matches.

points.text: Refreshes it and mentions it in the report

cards.title: Everything differs slightly
cards.text: Everything differs by a few pixels: likely font or animation instability.

points.text: Fix stability instead of reporting hundreds of changes
Mask a screen in config if it cannot be made stable

cards.title: Publishing fails
cards.text: The chosen target cannot publish.

points.text: Offers the artifact instead, or keeps local `index.html` and `report.md`

cards.title: Native apps
cards.text: Native capture (Capacitor, Expo/React Native) follows the documented simulator and emulator commands but has not been tried on a real app yet.

next_action.text: Commit your changes so the working tree is clean, then run `/ui-audit:capture` on your branch.
